key_insight: Co2In separates adaptive learning from persistent storage using working and long-term memory to balance acquisition of new knowledge with retention of prior knowledge.
engineering_relevance: The framework could inform continually updated engineering AI models, but the abstract provides no solid-mechanics or constitutive-modeling validation.
method: Encode new knowledge in working-memory network parameters.
Consolidate parameter patterns into a compact knowledge representation.
Transform representations and patterns into separate layers integrated into long-term memory.
evidence_signal: Evaluations on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and Tiny-ImageNet under exemplar-free Class-IL and Task-IL report state-of-the-art performance with efficient memory consumption.
watch_item: Memory growth across long task sequences and transfer to mechanics applications require further validation.
paper_title: Co2In: a Bi-level Memory Incremental Learning Framework with Knowledge Encoding, Consolidation, and Integration
